title: Lattice Blueprint
description: The contract between Blueprint (design time), Forge (build time) and Serve (query time). Forge and Serve make no ontology decisions; if either needs to decide what something means, this document is incomplete.

blueprint_version.description: Semver. Major: ontology changes requiring re-extraction. Minor: additive types. Patch: descriptions, patterns, non-semantic edits.

blueprint_hash.description: Content hash, computed by tooling over everything except this field. Stamped on every node and edge Forge writes, so a later blueprint change can target exactly the affected types instead of forcing a full rebuild.

design_note.description: Why each type exists. In six months someone will ask why two types were not merged and nobody will remember. Not optional in practice.

structure.description: How raw sources become chunks. Deterministic: no model involved.

hierarchy.description: Ordered outermost first. Each level's regex runs with MULTILINE. One capture group means the heading has no separate number and the group is the title; two means number then title.

example.description: A real line from the corpus this matched. Proves the pattern was tested, not guessed.

chunk_at.description: Which hierarchy level becomes a Chunk. Must name a declared level.

subsplit_pattern.description: Only applied above max_chunk_chars. Splitting short units cuts relations in half.

skip_regions.description: Front matter, tables of contents, indexes. These match heading patterns and produce chunks you pay to extract nothing from.

xref_patterns.description: Cross-references parsed deterministically at near-100% precision. Anything listed here must also appear in ontology.deterministic_relations so the extractor is told not to duplicate it.

closed.description: Always true. An open ontology is the single most common cause of a hairball graph. Forge sets every additional_* pruning flag from this.

node_types.description: 6 to 12 is the working range. Past ~15 the model is choosing between near-synonymous labels and the choice becomes arbitrary. If a domain seems to need 25, most of them are properties.

patterns.description: Domain/range signatures as [source, RELATION, target]. Exhaustive: a relationship with no declared pattern is unconstrained. This is the highest-leverage validation available, because a violating edge can be dropped without a human reading it.

deterministic_relations.description: Relations produced by structure.xref_patterns. The extractor is instructed to skip these.

vocabularies.description: Controlled lists for node types with many surface forms. Entities resolve against the list rather than pairwise against each other, because pairwise resolution drifts and anchoring does not.

seeded_from.description: Authoritative external source, e.g. USDA FoodData Central.

temporal.description: For corpora amended over time. Without validity intervals, superseded content answers queries and nobody notices until it matters.

dimensions.description: Must match the model exactly. A mismatch does not raise; it makes every search return nothing.

targets.description: What gets vectorised. Embedding raw chunk text alone loses the hierarchy: 'Article 12' is ambiguous without its path.

facet.description: Facet name when multi_vector is on, e.g. identity, flavor, ingredients.

multi_vector.description: Separate vectors per facet rather than one blended vector per node. Better on structured domains where a query targets one aspect.

hybrid.description: Fulltext alongside vectors. Matters more than people expect: users type exact identifiers and short rare terms, and vector similarity is mediocre at both.

workload.description: The questions this graph must answer. This is what makes the ontology falsifiable: without it, 'is this a good schema?' has no answer.

kind.description: lookup should match or lose to plain vector RAG; multi_hop is where the graph must win. Include at least one of each so the comparison is honest.

golden_set.description: Path to a JSONL of labelled questions. 30 to 50 is enough to steer decisions.

baseline.description: Measure plain vector RAG on the same corpus. GraphRAG costs more to build and run; if it does not beat the baseline on the declared shapes, the schema is wrong and more graph will not fix it.

guardrails.description: What must never leak. Decided at design time, compiled into Cypher at query time. A prompt-level constraint can be talked around; a WHERE clause cannot.

conflict_policy.description: Sources will disagree. surface_both with attribution is the safe default; a safety corpus may want the stricter rule to win. This is a domain decision and belongs here, not in Serve.

refuse_outside_corpus.description: Say 'not in the corpus' rather than falling back to general knowledge. For a corpus someone deliberately built a graph from, that fallback defeats the point.

release_blockers.description: Named eval suites that must pass before any release. Safety filters belong here.

drift.description: Thresholds that turn ontology maintenance from a vague worry into a triggered task with evidence attached.

require_page.description: Set for paginated sources where 'where does it say that' is a legitimate question.

description.description: Sent to the extractor on every chunk, so keep it tight once the profile is proven. Verbose descriptions are correct for the first run and wasteful afterwards.

answers.description: The user question this type exists to answer. A type that cannot name one is a property, not a node.
